title: Esterification
log: 2026-10-27T00:53:11Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Esterification
card: Esterification is the reaction of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol. It makes an ester and water: carboxylic acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water.

The reaction is slow and reversible. It needs a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid as a catalyst, and heat under reflux. Reflux means the mixture is boiled with a condenser fitted, so vapours cool and drip back into the flask.

The ester has a C=O group with an O joined to a carbon chain: the group is COO. The name has two parts. The first comes from the alcohol (methyl, ethyl) and the second from the acid (ethanoate, propanoate). Ethanoic acid and methanol make methyl ethanoate.

Many esters are volatile and have sweet, fruity smells. This is why they are used in flavourings and perfumes. The ester is the product, so the mixture ends up with a fruity smell that the acid and alcohol alone do not have.
draft.remember: Acid + alcohol ⇌ ester + water, using sulfuric acid and reflux.

a.q: Which pair of reactants, heated under reflux with concentrated sulfuric acid, makes ethyl propanoate?
a.why: The first part of the name, ethyl, comes from the alcohol ethanol. The second part, propanoate, comes from propanoic acid. Ethanoic acid with propan-1-ol is tempting, but it makes propyl ethanoate, as the parts are swapped.
a.clue: The alcohol gives the first word of the ester name.

b.q: Jun heats ethanol and ethanoic acid in a flask with a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid. He fits a condenser upright in the neck of the flask. What is the main reason for the condenser?
opts: It returns vapours to the flask so none are lost
It removes the water so the reaction goes to completion
It stops the reaction from reversing
It is the catalyst that makes the ester form
b.why: Under reflux, vapours of the reactants and product cool in the condenser and drip back into the flask, so the mixture can be heated for a long time without loss. The sulfuric acid is the catalyst, not the condenser. The condenser does not remove water.
b.clue: Think about what happens to hot vapours at the top of the flask.

b.best: It returns vapours to the flask so none are lost
